steps.name: Busy Shopkeeper
steps.text: Huh, you want to buy obsidian?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Mhm! I see you have all kinds of ores here... but no obsidian.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: I saw something about the Obsidian Festival on a flyer before... Isn't obsidian supposed to be a Siestan specialty?
The short man flips through a geology manual and shows the Obsidian Festival flyer enclosed within to the shopkeeper.
Next to the crumpled flyer is a sketch of the mineral that he drew himself.
The shopkeeper's nose is buried in the goods awaiting arrangement on the shelves, and he doesn't even lift his head to look.

steps.name: Busy Shopkeeper
steps.text: We can't go around selling the stuff openly, not after the Obsidian Festival.

steps.name: Busy Shopkeeper
steps.text: Try your luck elsewhere. I got nothing for you!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Wait, music festival? ...I've only heard of the regular Obsidian Festival.

spans.text: festival? ...I've only heard of the regular Obsidian Festival.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Is... it not a festival for selling obsidian?

steps.name: Busy Shopkeeper
steps.text: It's not. It's for music addicts to cut loose.

steps.name: Busy Shopkeeper
steps.text: Noisy as hell, day in, day out. At least it's finally over now.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Um... Would you happen to know where I can find some obsidian then?
The shopkeeper looks up from his hectic work and peers at the short fellow in front of him.
He is surprised at first, but then shows signs of displeasure.

steps.name: Busy Shopkeeper
steps.text: A kid? ...Didn't I say not to cause trouble at my place?

steps.name: Busy Shopkeeper
steps.text: I don't have any obsidian here, so run along back to your mommy now!
The shopkeeper slams the door shut, locks it from the inside, and draws the curtains.
The small man scratches his head.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Huh... Did I offend him somehow?

steps.name: Tourist
steps.text: It's probably because you mentioned obsidian.

steps.name: Tourist
steps.text: Some Siestans get real antsy the moment they hear that word, as if they're afraid it'll get them involved in something.

steps.name: Tourist
steps.text: Apparently there was a Catastrophe Messenger who hid the volcano's situation and completely tricked everyone.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: A Catastrophe Messenger... hiding the truth? But why?

steps.name: Tourist
steps.text: Why else? For the money. Long story short, so much obsidian was dug up that it destroyed the environment around the volcano, and now Siesta has to relocate...

steps.name: Tourist
steps.text: What a damn shame! When I think about that beautiful beach soon being swallowed up by lava... A tragedy is what it is! Maybe this is the unavoidable fate of the Siestans.

steps.name: Tourist
steps.text: So stop looking for obsidian and get a move on! What could possibly be more important than getting outta here before the whole volcano blows?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Destroying the environment, lying to the people, and inviting disaster...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: It's nothing like what the flyer said. Is obsidian really such a terrible mineral?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Also... if the Siestans knew in advance that the volcano was going to erupt and had already begun preparing accordingly, then why...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Why does everyone still seem so restless?

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: Heeheeheheheh... Lemme tell you something, kiddo. In the face of disaster, everyone's going to go through a mix of sensitivity, anxiety, and pain, no matter how well prepared they are.

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: That so-called 'preparation' is nothing more than a false sense of security, a coping mechanism... Heeheeheheh.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: ...What? Wh-Who are you?

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: Oh, that hardly matters. What matters is that I know your past. I've also grasped your present and glimpsed into your future.
A withered hand stretches out from under the sleeve, presenting a small bone plate.
The mysterious person wobbles the plate around, causing the metal balls upon it roll around, making an indescribable sound when they collide.
He then contorts himself into a strange posture, craning his neck to press his ear against the bone plate as if carefully interpreting some sort of message.

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: Ohohohoh... I hear it.

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: What a poor, pitiful child you are. From the day the disaster from the skies destroyed your 'burrows,' you were driven towards the frigid cold and scorching sun of the surface.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Burrows? They're not burrows, they're our cities. Underground cities. Have you never heard of Durins?

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: Durins? They're no different from us. We all have our fair share of worries and hardships throughout life.

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: I know what it is you're looking for, and what you're trying to protect. Do not heed the words of others; simply follow your heart, and do as you desire.
With the other hand, the person reaches inside his pocket to produce a small stone.
The jet-black crystal seems to absorb all sunlight, diffusing it across its lustrous surface.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Whoa... It's beautiful.

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: Instead of preparing for disaster, it is better to seek out refuge so that disaster may never again occur.

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: Heheheh... This chunk of obsidian will protect you, but... only if you're willing to pay a small 'price.'

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: (This black stone is certainly quite beautiful... but it doesn't feel like a natural mineral at all.)

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: (Is it really obsidian?)

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: (For all I know, it could just be a piece of glass.)

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Excuse me, sir—

steps.name: Tourist A
steps.text: Oh, I found it! Over here!

steps.name: Tourist B
steps.text: Finally, there you are! The swindler with the bone plate!

steps.name: Tourist B
steps.text: Trying to scam people with fake goods?! You call this obsidian?

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: Absolutely. What I sell is 'obsidian'! These are all spiritual stones that ensure peoples' safety. Once sold, they cannot be returned!

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: If what you're after is that accursed rock that brings only calamity, then go dig it up yourself from that volcanic cave!

steps.name: Tourist A
steps.text: You bastard! Give us back our money, now!
The situation before the short man devolves into a brawl.
The tourists' wallets, the mysterious person's bone plate, and a button ripped from someone's shirt all fly through the air and land nearby.
Along with the 'obsidian,' rolling to a stop at the short man's feet.
He leans over and picks it up.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: It turned darker...
He takes out the 'obsidian' he had just obtained earlier from his specimen box.
The piece of black glass sinks into the darkness of the cave, and it becomes hard to distinguish its outline.
The short man waves his staff around, brightening the area.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: The bone plate guy gave me directions to the real obsidian mine as a thank-you for pulling the two angry tourists off of him.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: It should be right here.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Though this mine's really old, some company has been active here for quite some time, and the ore in the shallow layer is likely on the verge of exhaustion.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: But this place should be safe enough, based on how far it is from the volcano... In any case, I won't know if I can find any obsidian here until I try.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Hmm... Actually, I really need to take a closer look at the geological structure of this cave. These fine, regularly-spaced lines... Were they left behind by lava flows? The thin line bends here, then extends downward...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: ...Which likely means I still need to go a bit deeper. The veins containing ore should be farther down.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: That sound... is that water? ...No.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Behind the pillar... Who's there? Why are you hiding?

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: What, it's just a little kid.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: I'm not a kid! I'm a grown adult!
The man frowns.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: What'd you come here for? You don't just waltz into an obsidian mine. It's dangerous down here.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: I'm looking for obsidian veins... I'm a geological surveyor of sorts?

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Tch, a surveyor, huh?

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Where are you from, Victoria or Columbia? What geological institute do you belong to? Or are you with one of those high-and-mighty conservation organizations?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: You've got the wrong idea, sir... I'm not here on behalf of any organization. Collecting beautiful rocks like obsidian is just a personal hobby.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Hold on... Gah, too bright! Point that thing away from me! What are you doing?!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: ...Abnormal ridges around the fingernails, and sclera show signs of yellowing, which either means you have some problem with your digestive system, or you haven't eaten in a while.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Also...
The short man raises his staff, and a faint glow pours out in front of it.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Wh-What's going on? I feel... warmth.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: You've sprained your leg. Don't worry though, I'll help relieve the muscle fatigue and repair the damaged tissue.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: How do you feel now?

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Much better. It doesn't seem to hurt anymore. Are you a doctor, little fella?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: I don't qualify as a doctor yet, but I do know some basic healing Arts.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: This light can only temporarily relieve your symptoms. If the problems come back and the pain gets worse, you should go see a specialist.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Mm... Appreciate it.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Here, I'll help you up.
The short man reaches over to help pull up the person lying in the corner, but his body is heavier than expected.
He manages to help the man stand up, but the force from being pulled forward nearly makes him topple over.
The little piece of black glass tucked in his pocket falls to the ground with a clinking sound.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Ah! My 'obsidian'!

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Obsidian?

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Isn't that one of those cheap knock-offs made by Siestan hawkers to trick tourists?

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: They told you this was obsidian?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Uhh... Actually, I knew all along that it was a fake.
The man leans over and picks up the black rock that had fallen onto the ground, pinches it between his thumb and index finger, then taps it against the wall to produce another clinking sound.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Please don't mess with it any more...

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: What's the big deal? Isn't this just a piece of black glass? Completely worthless.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Here, take it.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Yes, but even if it isn't obsidian, it still counts as a beautiful stone.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Every stone has its own value.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: What a strange little fella.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: How about I show you something actually worth something?
The man takes off the cloth bag fastened to his waist and unties the rope. It's filled to the brim with black rocks.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Here, all of this obsidian is yours.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Whoa! This is... it's all real obsidian! But...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: You're giving all these to me? Why...?

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: As thanks for the treatment you just gave me.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Oh... But I don't need all that. I just wanted a little chunk to study in my collection. Just this one's fine.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: You came all the way into this mine just for a tiny little chunk of obsidian... for your collection? To study? You sure?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: One piece is enough. Combined with the lava markings left in the cave, I have a pretty good idea of where the obsidian veins are.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: What do you need the veins for? Is a whole bag of the stuff not enough for you?

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Just take it before I change my mind. Won't get a deal this good anywhere.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: But... isn't all this more valuable to you? I mean, you took a whole lot of risks just to come dig it up.

spans.text: But... isn't all this more valuable to
? I mean, you took a whole lot of risks just to come dig it up.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Oh! I, um... Yeah, I won't tell anyone! Especially not anyone on the lookout for obsidian smugglers.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Also... I won't be in Siesta much longer, now that I've got my hands on the real deal.

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: What, you think I'm a smuggler just 'cause of this bag here?

steps.name: Cautious Man
steps.text: Lots of people come here looking for obsidian. Volcanologists, environmental workers, government employers... and folks like you, surveyors who are 'just interested.'

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: If you really were some kind of researcher here to monitor volcanic activity, why wouldn't you shout for help when you saw someone coming?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: You hurt your leg and couldn't move, plus it looks like you've been down here without food for quite some time now...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: But even after I found you, you were more worried about who I might be, rather than how I could help you.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: So what else could explain all that, other than being an obsidian smuggler?

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Smuggling? What the hell are you talking about? ...My old man was an obsidian miner, so's my brother, and so am I.

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: This is how we make a living. How does that add up to 'smuggling'?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Sir... I meant no offense. I'm not qualified to judge Siesta's policies or your actions, nor am I in any position to do so, but...

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Doesn't matter anyway.

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Even if you go running off to tell the police or the people at City Hall or whatever, this is what I gotta do to support my family.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: But what if the volcano suddenly erupts early?

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Who cares? That's way off in the future. How could that happen all of a sudden?

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Besides, the Siestans have already started moving, so there's still plenty of time.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: ...But wouldn't it be way too late by the time disaster actually struck?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: My old hometown was destroyed in a sudden disaster. Everything we had worked so hard to build was just gone overnight.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: In order to find out what caused it, my people and I started studying geology. Afterwards, I came to the surface to see how various other people handle their crises.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Seeing Catastrophe Messengers warning people of danger, nomadic cities moving people away from high-risk areas... I really admire that kind of resilience.

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Resilience? What do you mean by that?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Hmm... I mean being able to bounce back after facing a sudden crisis?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Just like a huge lake. Not only can it store the runoff from a flooding river after a rainy season, but it can also nourish that same river during droughts.

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: In that case, why don't you people move to a nomadic city like Siesta, too?

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: If they're all as observant as you, I'm sure you could easily pick out a few capable people to be Catastrophe Messengers.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Well... Um, there are actually a lot of things we don't quite understand.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Compared to my hometown, Siesta's a pretty lucky city. After all, the volcano hasn't erupted yet, and there's still plenty of time to avoid the brunt of the disaster.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Busy Shopkeeper
steps.text: I don't have any obsidian here, so run along back to your mommy now!

steps.name: Tourist
steps.text: Maybe this is the unavoidable fate of the Siestans... What could possibly be more important than getting outta here before the whole volcano blows?

steps.name: Mysterious Person
steps.text: That so-called 'preparation' is nothing more than a false sense of security, a coping mechanism... Heeheeheheh.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Even knowing about the disaster doesn't seem to be making life any easier for the Siestans...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: So what do we do...? What can we do when faced with these sudden natural disasters?

spans.text: So what do we do...? What
we do when faced with these sudden natural disasters?

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Wh-What's going on? It's shaking so much... Don't tell me the volcano's actually about to blow...?

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: I just had to jinx it... There's no way our timing's actually this bad, is there?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: No, I don't think it should erupt just yet...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: But the structure of this cave is already extremely unstable, and even the slightest volcanic activity could cause it to collapse.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: We need to get out of here, now.

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: ...Hah, I reckon that's easier said than done.
A swarm of Originium slugs starts approaching from the cave's entrance.

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: If we head over there, they'll pick our bones clean!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Head down! Follow me!

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Well, what now? There are slugs down there too. Stop going down and take that higher passage up there!

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: I'm familiar with that area. Mined obsidian up there a few times! Besides, didn't you say you wanted to check out the obsidian veins? Well, now's your chance!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Let's keep going this way.

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Is that some kinda sick joke? I ain't dying down here with you!

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: I'm going that way.
Before the miner finishes his words, the wall above that cave passage cracks open, and an Originium slug squeezes out from it.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: This way! Over here! What are you even doing?

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Oh... Coming...

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Could you tell it was dangerous that way?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: I know it looks like we're going deeper right now, but I can tell from the lines on the wall that it'll climb back up as we go forward. Plus... the Originium slugs aren't coming this way.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: As for the path up there... Didn't you just say that you mined obsidian from there?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Long-term excavation will absolutely destroy the stability of the rock formation, and it could easily collapse if things start shaking again. Also, after the ore gets dug out, the cavity left behind is the perfect place for a slug nest.

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Heh. You've got a little bit of that magic in you, little man.

steps.name: Obsidian Miner
steps.text: Treating the wounded, observing the environment, guiding an escape, slug-related disasters... Do you do this all the time?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: I see light ahead! That should be our way out!
After escaping from the mines, Chestnut says goodbye to the obsidian miner.
'Do you do this all the time?'
But disaster still struck... when nobody was ready for it.
The short man cannot help but think: what else can he do? For now, he still can't come up with an answer.
However, he now welcomes two new guests to his specimen box — two pieces of beautiful 'obsidian.' That was enough to make him feel at peace.
On his last day in Siesta, Chestnut went to the beach, drank ice-cold soda from a street vendor, felt the sea breeze, and listened to the sound of the waves.
Sitting on the stone steps, he opens up his booklet and starts detailing the hard-earned ore in his hand, recording this unique holiday in the way he's accustomed to.
This time, though, the sound of crying suddenly pierces through the momentary calm of the receding waves.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Is that a little kid?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Is it coming from the beach?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Uwaaaaah—

steps.name: Little Boy
steps.text: Hey! Stop crying! What's the big deal anyway?!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: ...Excuse me, what's wrong?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Waaaaah—

steps.name: Little Boy
steps.text: A big wave just came and messed up our drawing of our big brother!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: A drawing of your big brother? Where is it?

steps.name: Little Boy
steps.text: Right under your foot.
Chestnut looks down and sees that he's stepping on a drawing in the sand.
Even though it had been washed away by the waves, he can vaguely see the outline of a large head.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Um... How about we draw another one? I can help you out.

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Uwaaaaaaaaaah!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Huh? Why's she crying even harder now?

steps.name: Little Boy
steps.text: We can't! Big brother's eyes have been washed away!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: His eyes? Why not just draw two more?

steps.name: Little Boy
steps.text: No, the eyes have to be rocks. My little sis went all over the beach looking for the right ones, and finally found two round black pebbles, but the waves took them away!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: *sniffle*...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Black pebbles?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: How about these? Will they work?
Chestnut holds out two chunks of obsidian—one real, one fake. The two children come closer and carefully look them over.

steps.name: Little Boy
steps.text: Um... This might work?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: No, no...

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Huh? That's too bad then...

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: They... They're not round enough!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Oh, I've got you.
His staff is once again surrounded with light, which then wraps around the two 'black pebbles.'

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: The rocks... are round now?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: So now we've got the eyes. What else do we need?

steps.name: Little Boy
steps.text: Draw a big ol' head!

steps.name: Little Girl
steps.text: I'll draw the ears, and he'll draw the mouth... Since you're new here, you can just put the eyes in!

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: You want me to do it?

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Hmm, these two rocks...
The short man places the two 'black pebbles' inside the sand portrait, and the sound of the children's laughter drifts into his ears.

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: Under the sunlight, the way they shine... isn't any different.
But, that's not important anymore—
Right now, they are bright, shining eyes.

steps.name: Little Girl & Little Boy
steps.text: Now it's perfect!
The portrait in the sand slowly becomes more and more complete. Apparently, in the minds of these two kids, the brother is... a bit funny-looking.
Phew...
Is it time to head home? To return underground, to return to my people, to build a stronger home together?
The waves may still surge over onto the beach, mercilessly washing away our masterpiece without warning.
But, the big ol' head can be drawn again. And you can always find two more 'black pebbles.'

steps.name: Chestnut
steps.text: This time... should be perfect, right?
